Subject: Metering question: partial streaming tokens + retries

Hi Priyom,

We're building an integration that streams model output to our UI. A few technical questions came up from engineering and procurement while we review the contract:

- If a streaming response disconnects mid-generation (client drops connection or network blip) and we retry the same request, how are tokens billed? Do partial tokens from the first interrupted stream count?
- If the server returns a partial chunk and we re-request the same prompt (idempotent retry), do you treat that as a new generation for billing purposes?
- Any recommended idempotency best practices or headers to avoid double billing?

We're also pulling together baseline hosted API rate expectations for finance — can you attach the current rate card and confirm whether streaming is priced differently than non-streaming for per-token metering? Attaching our draft MSA for reference.

Thanks,
Alicia

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (pricing lead) and our infra lead for the exact enforcement mechanics. Attaching our current rate card (xlsx) so finance has the headline numbers. Quick answers up front:

- We generally bill for tokens that were emitted by the model runtime, including partial chunks, unless a transient platform error causes a guaranteed retry credit.
- Idempotent retries can avoid duplicate billings if you provide an idempotency token and we detect the same request within a short window — we have a specific policy on that; Marissa will fill in the thresholds.
- Streaming itself does not have a separate per-token rate, but streaming enables token-level incremental delivery and may change how you think about retry windows and prefix caching.

Next: Marissa — can you confirm the exact idempotency window, retry credit thresholds, and any discounting options for committed volume?

Marissa / Priyom — drafting the technical + billing policy below so you can paste into procurement email. TL;DR: emitted tokens are charged; we can issue credits for platform-caused failures; idempotency keys can prevent double billing within a 2-minute window. Details:

Billing definition:
- Billed tokens: any token the runtime successfully generates and commits to the model output buffer. If a chunk is emitted to the network (even if client disconnects before acknowledging), the token counts as billed.
- Partial-chunk handling: we charge on emission boundaries. If a chunk contains partial token bytes due to encoding fragmentation, we round to token boundaries before billing.

Retries and idempotency:
- Idempotency: Accept an "Idempotency-Key" header (string) for streaming requests. If we receive a request with the same key and identical prompt payload within a 120-second window, we do not bill the second request for tokens already emitted by the prior request; instead we stream the cached output or resume. This requires using the same model & generation config.
- Retries without idempotency: treated as a new request and billed normally.

Platform error credits:
- If a request fails due to platform error (node preemption, kernel crash, internal timeout) we issue an automatic credit for that request for all tokens billed by that request. Credits are applied to the next invoice and flagged in the Console.
- If failure is caused by client disconnects or application-level retries, credits are not automatic; we handle these case-by-case with tickets.

Commercial notes (pricing):
- Streaming vs non-streaming: single per-token rate applies; streaming does not carry a premium.
- Baseline hosted API rate (list): see attached ratecard. Example: $0.0008 per token for standard models, $0.0016 per token for large-context models.
- Commit discounts: we can offer tiered discounts on top of the ratecard for 12-month commitments. Example bands: 10% at $50k/month commit, 18% at $150k/month, custom pricing above $500k/month.

Operational recommendations for FinLedger:
- Use Idempotency-Key on all client-initiated retries.
- Add a short client-side buffer (2–3s) to allow reconnect/resume paths and reduce premature re-requests.
- Instrument and surface request ids in logs; we can reconcile charges quickly with request ids and idempotency keys.

References:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/FinLedger
- Ratecard: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz/redwood-ratecard-jan2026

Happy to convert into a one-paragraph statement for procurement.

Hi Alicia / Tom — thanks for your patience. Consolidating our position below (you can share this with your procurement/legal team):

Short answer: tokens are billed when the runtime emits them. Streaming does not change per-token pricing. We provide an "Idempotency-Key" mechanism and limited-time deduplication to avoid double billing on retries, and we also credit requests that fail due to platform errors.

Key points to share with procurement:
- Billing: any token the model emits is billed. Partial network disconnects that happen after emission are not billed differently.
- Idempotency: include an Idempotency-Key header. If the same request (same prompt and gen config) arrives with the same key within 120s, we will avoid re-billing tokens already emitted and will attempt to resume/stream cached output instead.
- Platform failures: automatic credit for platform-caused failures (applied to next invoice). Client-caused disconnects require a support ticket for review.
- Pricing: use the attached ratecard for per-token rates (streaming uses the same per-token rates as non-streaming).
- Commercial: we can discuss a first-year commitment discount; Marissa will follow up with detailed pricing bands and a formal commercial term you can insert into the MSA.

Next steps:
- Marissa will send an official pricing addendum and the exact idempotency header spec.
- If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute call between your engineering and our runtime team to walk through reconnect/resume best practices.

Would you like to lock a time next week?
